verdicts.summary: The status waiter's wait is capped at 5s. Fetches for the same key are deduplicated without a race, and the map entry is deleted inside the fiber's own onExit, before any new fetch for that key can be added.
verdicts.scenario: I tried two polls for the same key running at the same time, and a new fetch replacing one that had just finished. The lookup and the set (1283-1310) run in one synchronous uninterruptible block, so two fetches for one key cannot both start. The old fiber removes its entry before it exits (1303-1306). That means a new entry can only be added after the old one is gone, so the old fiber's cleanup cannot delete the new entry. A failed fetch records its back-off (1300) before the fiber exits, so the cache's TTL (1555) sees the new failure count. When the waiter hits its timeout (1314-1315) it stops waiting, but the background fetch keeps running.

verdicts.summary: The only hazard is the unbounded Fiber.await(pending) at line 2670, which finding 0 already reports. The retry's guards (one merge ref, same branch, HEAD unchanged at 2715-2721) stop it from pulling into a checkout that has moved.
A number passed as forceKillAfter is read as milliseconds. When the option is undefined, the default SIGTERM-then-wait path runs as before.
verdicts.scenario: I tried the case where the value is missing: line 969 sets forceKillAfter to undefined, and Predicate.isUndefined at 484 sends it to the old one-second grace wait. I also tried the number 1_000: Duration.toMillis calls fromInputUnsafe, which turns a number into millis (Duration.ts:242-245), so the escalation to SIGKILL fires after 1s.
